**Top of mind:** Snorkel AI just closed a $350M round at a $3.5B valuation — nearly 3x its May 2025 mark — with CEO Alex Ratner telling Reuters that "100% of the data that labs will get value out of will have some human input in the foreseeable future" even as synthetic/automated methods scale alongside it. It's the clearest signal yet that investor appetite for the training-data layer is accelerating, not cooling, and it puts fresh competitive pressure on Scale AI, Mercor, and Surge AI, all chasing the same frontier-lab budgets.

## Competitor moves
- **Snorkel AI triples valuation to $3.5B on a $350M raise.** Insight Partners and S32 co-led, with Addition, Greylock, and Wells Fargo returning; annualized revenue run-rate jumped from ~$20M to $350M+, driven largely by the data-as-a-service line launched a year ago and by coding-data demand. For anyone selling human-in-the-loop data services, this is the strongest proof point yet that money and multiples are flowing to complex, expert-grade labeling rather than commodity annotation — and the piece explicitly names Mercor and Surge AI as rivals also pulling in investor interest right now. [Reuters via The Daily Guardian](https://thedailyguardian.com/news/science-tech/exclusive-snorkel-ai-valued-at-3-5-billion-amid-surging-demand-for-complex-ai-training-data-759270/), [Reuters via 93.3 The Drive](https://www.933thedrive.com/2026/09/22/exclusive-snorkel-ai-valued-at-3-5-billion-amid-surging-demand-for-complex-ai-training-data/)

## Frontier lab movements
- **OpenAI forms a 9-person Mathematics & AI advisory board after claiming 100+ solved problems.** Fields medalists Terence Tao, Timothy Gowers and Martin Hairer, plus Edward Witten, will vet claims that an internal model resolved 100+ long-standing open math problems in 24 days. It's effectively a frontier lab outsourcing high-end verification and evaluation work to credentialed domain experts — a template that could extend to other technical domains where labeling firms already place specialist talent. [TechCrunch](https://techcrunch.com/2026/09/21/openai-forms-math-advisory-group-as-its-ai-resolves-more-than-100-open-problems/), [Terence Tao's blog](https://terrytao.wordpress.com/2026/09/21/advisory-group-on-mathematics-and-artificial-intelligence/)
- **Anthropic confirms a physical Bay Area wet lab for AI-directed biology experiments.** Built on top of its $400M Coefficient Bio acquisition, the lab pairs Claude with real experiments and launches a Life Sciences Verification Program giving vetted researchers tiered model access. Another sign frontier labs need specialized, credentialed human expertise — not generic crowdwork — to validate scientific outputs, which is a growth lane for data/eval vendors with domain-expert networks. [Reuters coverage via AI Weekly](https://aiweekly.co/alerts/anthropic-confirms-bay-area-wet-lab-for-biology-experiments), [80.lv](https://80.lv/articles/claude-creator-anthropic-sets-up-wet-lab-for-biology-research)

## Research papers
- **"1% of Tokens Can Be Enough" shows on-policy distillation needs far less supervision.** Sheng, Ye, Wang, Wang, Gu and Kang introduce an Information-Efficiency Ratio (IER) that selects which tokens deserve teacher supervision, matching full on-policy distillation while supervising just 0.1–1% of tokens on math and medical reasoning tasks. If it generalizes, it directly cuts teacher-model inference costs and the volume of labeled/reviewed tokens labs need to buy — worth watching as a potential headwind on per-token annotation demand. [arXiv:2609.24432](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.24432)
- **onPanda cuts alignment-annotation time ~52% with token-level correction.** Lei Yang et al.'s "locate-correct-continue" workflow has annotators fix only the first problematic token instead of full post-editing, preserving the model's natural output distribution for cleaner preference/SFT data; the team also released the Panda-CVL dataset and an agent-trajectory annotation benchmark. This is a direct efficiency lever for RLHF/SFT labeling throughput and margins — the kind of tooling that reshapes unit economics rather than volume. [arXiv:2609.24983](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.24983)

## Research papers

- **CodeMidas: Scaling Agentic Coding RL Environments from Code Itself** (Ye, Li, Li, Yue, Zhang, Lv, Liu, Ma, Tian, Li, Dong, Zhao, Deng, Zhang, Zhao, Liu, Kong, Yang, Luo — Sept 18, 2026). Auto-generates 5,545 reinforcement-learning tasks from 3,185 real codebases and uses them to train the MiMo-V2.5 coding agent via GRPO, lifting scores +11.7% on DeepSWE and +17% on ProgramBench — a template for turning raw code repositories into scalable, self-supervised training environments instead of hand-labeled data, relevant to anyone selling agentic-coding eval/RL-environment work. [arXiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.22068) · [Hugging Face Papers](https://huggingface.co/papers/2609.22068)

## Research papers

- **"Learning Heterogeneous Preferences"** (Shiwali Mohan, Matt Hong, Dule Shu, Aniek Fransen, Shabnam Hakimi, Matt Klenk) challenges the standard RLHF assumption of one universal reward function, instead fitting "individuated utility functions" per annotator and context. Tested on aesthetic judgments from 2,300+ raters, individuated models substantially beat universal ones — a direct argument for how labeling companies should structure and weight annotator pools rather than averaging away disagreement. [arXiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.17847) — submitted Sept 15, 2026
- **"Benchmark Radar: A Living Database and Search Engine for AI Benchmarks and Evaluation"** (Koutian Wu, Junjie Zhou, Ergan Shang, Jiayu Wang, Pengqian Han, Junkai Wang, Wanghan Xu, Lin Shi) aggregates 1,283 benchmark records and ~13,000 observations with leaderboard and saturation tracking — a useful competitive-intelligence tool for eval-focused data companies to see which benchmarks are gaining or losing relevance. [arXiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.11115) — v1 Sept 10, v2 Sept 13, 2026
- **"What Do We Expect from LLMs? Mapping the Design of LLM Benchmarks"** examines how benchmark design is evolving as LLM-as-judge scoring expands relative to human- and model-generated eval material — relevant to the argument that human evaluators and labelers need to stay load-bearing in eval pipelines rather than being fully automated away. [arXiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.19182) — submitted Sept 19, 2026

## Research papers

- **Synthetic pretraining cuts Devanagari handwriting-annotation needs by about 4.4x.** Manglesh Kumar Pandey and Sumit Kumar Banshal show that supervised synthetic pretraining lets a Devanagari handwriting recognizer match baseline accuracy using only 81 hand-transcribed word images instead of 355, a concrete data-efficiency technique directly applicable to Indic-script annotation pipelines. [arXiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.16859)
- **Yale-led re-grading finds physics benchmarks were broken, not the models.** A large expert author team (Ali Ansari, John Sous, Arman Cohan and 40+ co-authors, Yale University) manually re-graded six major physics benchmarks and found most "wrong" answers actually reflected flawed reference solutions or ambiguous questions, reinforcing that rigorous expert review, not raw benchmark scores, is what separates real evaluation quality. [arXiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.13009)
